title: Why AI Didn't Actually Make You Ship Faster — Gabriel Spencer-Harper, Meticulous
talk_summary: A Meticulous founder argues that AI code generation has shifted the bottleneck to verification, and pitches exhaustive front-end verification via recorded browser flows replayed in CI with mocked network, deterministic browser scheduling, and screenshot diffs at every atomic moment. The transferable ideas are coverage-driven test selection, determinism-by-mocking to kill flakes, and showing diffs rather than pass/fail assertions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Record many real user flows, replay each once against main while monitoring executed lines, build a workflow-to-lines index, then pick the subset of flows that maximizes code coverage for PR runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we build a map or an index that maps each individual workflow to lines lines of code executed and choose a subset of workflows that maximizes code coverage

takeaways.technique: Mock network at record time for determinism
takeaways.what_they_do: Record all network requests/responses during a session and stub them at replay, making tests idempotent and isolated so they can be parallelized horizontally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at record time we record all the network requests and responses and then at replay time we stub those in

takeaways.what_they_do: Augment the browser from the scheduling layer up to remove randomness (clock speed, setTimeout/setInterval interleaving) so replays are near-deterministic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we augment the browser from the scheduling engine layer up to be fully deterministic

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asserting pass/fail, the tool presents before/after diffs of every atomic state so a human or agent exercises judgment at review time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Meticulus will not tell you whether or not there's a bug. What it will show you is a set of diffs

takeaways.technique: Coverage as a proxy only when every state is checked
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue code coverage is a bad metric unless you screenshot at every atomic moment, because a test can cover 100% of code with one assertion; their screenshot-per-moment makes coverage approximate testing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code covered is not the same as code tested

takeaways.what_they_do: Frames verification capacity, not generation, as the constraint once agents write code fast; without exhaustive verification you trade velocity against bugs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI writes code faster than humans can review it. And review and verification is now the new bottleneck.
